FOREWORD This Indian Standard ( First Revision ) was adopted by the Bureau of Indian Standards, after the draft finalized by the Bulk Handling Systems and Equipment Sectional Committee had been approved by the Heavy Mechanical Engineering Division Council. Many products such as cement, fertilizer, foodgrains, etc, are handled in bags of varying capacities for convenience in handling, storage and marketing. Bag filling machines and bag stitching machines are employed by these industries. It has been found that usage in industry requires bag stitching machines for continuous heavy industrial duty and intermittent light industrial duty. Continuous heavy industrial machines are those machines which can operate continuously for longer duration in an industry. Intermittent light industrial duty machines are those machines which will work for a very short duration and then will stop to work on the next bag/batch of bags. Normally intermittent light industrial duty machines are portahlc and manually held for stitching operations. This Indian Standard which covers the general rcquircmcnts for industrtal bag stttching machtnes may serve as guidelines to the manufacturers and the users in the manufacture, sclcction and use of such machines. This standard was first published in 1986. In this revision, hag stitching machines of intermittent light industrial duty have been excluded. Other modifications include change in operating voltage, provision for reversing switch for conveyor, stitching speed, sequence of testing, etc. For the purpose of deciding whether a particular requirement of this standard is complied with, the final value, observed or calculated, expressing the result of a test or analysis, shall be rounded off in accordance with IS 2 : 1960 `Rules for rounding off numerical values (revised )`. The number of significant places retained in the rounded off value should be the same as that of the specified value in this standard.

1 SCOPE
1.1 This standard covers the general requirements for stitching machines designed for operation by electric motor for industrial purposes for closing small, medium and large size bags of jute, cotton, burlap, multiwall paper and synthetic materials. 1.1.1 This standard covers the requirement of bag closing machines consisting of stitching head, drive motor, supporting structure and controls for continuous heavy duty industrial application. 2 REFERENCES The following Indian Standards are necessary adjuncts to this standard: IS No. 325 : 1978 1068 : 1968 Title Three phase induction (second revision) motors

3.2.2 All electricals and controls shall be suitable for use in the classification of the area as specified by the purchaser. 3.3 Switch Unless otherwise specified, each machine shall have an integrally operated switch for starting and stopping the motor by the pressure of the bag or any other suitable arrangement when the bag is inserted into the machine. Alternatively,a foot switch for non-integrated or semi-automatic function may be provided if so specified. 3.3.1 A reversing switch for the filled bag con-

veyor reversing shall also be provided along with all other controls. 3.4 Drive Transmission Drive transmission from the motor to the stitching mechanism shall be either by gears or by V-belts. When V-belts are provided, provision shall be made for adjusting the belt tension without disturbing the belt alignment. Pulleys and belts shall be suitably guarded and so arranged as not to interfere with the operation of the machine. 4 SEWING MECHANISM 4.1 Design M'achine shall be ol' single needle design. quipped with 3 bcwing mcchani~m I'or producing C 11 ur D 12 stitch l'ormatiun 1 C 11 l'or single threaded chain stitch and D 12 for double threaded double lock stitch (see Fig. l)] in accordance with IS 9152 : 1979. 3.1 The machine shall be supplied with a motor, starting switch and controller. Interconnecting wiring between starter, controller and motor shall be installed in a suitable conduit or in Flexible metallic conduit. Electric light fixture may also be provided, if required. 3.2 The motor shall be suitable for operating on a 41.5 V, three phase, 50 hertz alternating current. The starting characteristics of the motor shall suit the driven machine. The rating of the motor shall be such as to ensure that its full load current is not exceeded under normal operating conditions. The design of the motor shall take into account up to 1 200 start-stops per hour depending upon the requirement. The motor shall conform to IS 325 : 1978.

4.2 Stitch Regulator The stitch regulator shall be conveniently located in the machine. It shall preferably be capable of adjusting the pitch of the stitch within a range of 6 mm to 12 mm as specified by the purchaser. 4.3 Automatic thread cutting.arrangement shall be provided on the machine to cut off the thread when stitching is completed. 4.4 Normal stitching speed of the machine shall be as agreed to between the purchaser and the manufacturer but shall not be less than 5 m/min or exceed 20 m/min. 4.5 A thread tension arrangement shall be provided with each machine for both lower and upper threads. It shall be adjustable to the amount of tension required to sew satisfactory stitches. Each machine shall be equipped with an automatic thread tension mechanism. 4.6 Thread Stand A thread stand shall be provided for the stitching machine to hold the thread cone at a convenient location on the machine. 5 COMPONENTS Components shall conform to relevant Standards to the extent applicable. 6 LUBRICATION Means shall be provided to readily and properly apply lubricant to all bearings and frictional sur2 Indian

7.1 The stitching machine shall be suitable for mounting on portable trolley or pedestal with suitable provision for height adjustment. 7.2 Portable mounting trolleys shall be rigidly built to avoid undue vibration and flexure during operation and at the same lime shall be easily portable. 7.2.1 Portable mounting trolleys shall be provided with rubber castor wheels. Size of the wheel shall be determined on the basis for its easy mobility without affecting the stability of the unit. 7.2.2 Sharp projections and ends shall be avoided on the trolleys. A handle at operatable height shall be provided for pushing the trolley. 7.3 It is recommended that a tool box to contain spare needles and tools for minor adjustments and normal maintenance of the machine may be provided. 8 CONSTRUCTION 8.1 Stitching machine and accessories shall be of rigid construction.

IS 11737 : 1996 8.2 The mass of the stitching head shall be kept to a minimum for the purpose of convenience in handling the unit. 8.3 Main body of the stitching machine shall be made of aluminium/aluminium alloy or other metals without impairing the strength and rigidity. 8.4 The holding handle shall be of a size to provide adequate grip and comfort. 9 WORKMANSHIP AND FINISH 9.1 Stitching machine and accessories shall be neat in appearance. They shall be free from objectionable vibrations and shall be quiet in operation. 9.2 Painted surfaces shall be hard and smooth, free from irregularities, flaws and cracks, dust specks and other defects. The paint shall be uneffccted by lubricating oils and not liable to soften at temperatures up to SOOC. 9.3 Plating Nickel and chromium plated surfaces shall satisfy the following conditions: a) Colour and lustre shall be good; b) Surface shall be smooth and free from plating defects, such as blisters, pits, cloudy patches, cracks and stains; Cl Coating shall not peel off easily; and d) Thickness of plating shall not be less than 0.015 mm (see IS 1068 : 1968). 10 TESTS 10.1 No Load Test The stitching machine shall be run continuously for eight hours at its rated speed on no load. The machine shall not show any signs of overheating, breakage or any other manufacturing defect. This test shall be carried out at the manufacturer's premises. `10.2 Run Test The stitching machine shall be run for half an hour for stitching the bags. The machine shall not show any signs of overheating, breakage or any other manufacturing defect. This test shall be carried out at the manufacturer's premises. 10.3 Performance Test
Works

for complete width of the bag, consecutively and following shall be verified: a) Tightness ofthe stitch - All stitches shall be tight to provide a leakfree sealing; b) Pitch of all the stitches shall be uniform. There shall not be a variation of more than 1 mm from the specified pitch; c) There shall be no'skip stitching; and d) There shall be no unusual thread breaking; e) Form of stitch shall be verified in accordance with 4.1 and Fig. 1. 10.3.2 Test at Site To check the performance of the stiching machine and of the components used, the machineshall be run continuously for eight hours at its rated speed on load. After this run, the machine shall not show any overheating, breakage or any other manufacturing defect. This test shall be carried out at site. 10.4 General Requirement The stitching machine shall have smooth movement without any abnormal sound. 11 ACCESSORIES 11.1 Following accessories shall be supplied with each machine: One spanner; One oil can/grease gun (to suit the lubricab) tion requirement of the machine); Two screw drivers; d) Four thread cones; e) Four needles; and f) A booklet containing the manufacturer's operatmg and mamtenance instructtons, exploded view of the machine and parts list with identification numbers.

Tools and accessories shall be placed in an accessories box placed in the wooden packing box in such a way that it does not directly come into contact with the machine parts. 13.2 The stitching unit shall be given a dampproof flexible covering before packing it in the wooden box to protect it from getting damped during transit and storage. 13.3 The box shall be securely fastened in a closed position to prevent opening while in transit. Top side of the packing shall be indicated using the word `TOP' with a standard symbol, such as an umbrella, cup, arrow, etc.

13 PACKING 13.1 All parts of the machine and the suspension unit shall be packed in suitable packing boxes and shall be securely fastened in fixed position to prevent movement or vibration during transit.
